How the reference pictures align with the target video — Picture 1 aligns with the 0.00-second mark of the target video; Picture 2 aligns with the 15.08-second mark of the target video.

integrated_multimodal_description: Fixed-lens architectural visualization, hyper-stable photorealistic drone shot in natural daylight. Perfect architectural integrity and rigid structural geometry maintained continuously from start to finish without any warping, bending, or shifting of walls and lines. The video is a single, perfectly smooth, unbroken camera glide from left to right along the western facade of the multi-story modern house. Zero camera jitter, zero frame tearing, zero spatial morphing. The camera begins at the South-West corner matching <Picture 1> and follows an ultra-smooth, uniform mathematical arc trajectory toward the North-West corner. Crisp architectural details, straight vertical pillars, fixed window frames, and stable perspective remain completely locked and rigid throughout the entire duration, ending precisely in the final framing of <Picture 2> at the 15.08-second mark.

overall_soundscape: Soft, low hum of drone propellers blended with a quiet, peaceful ambient atmosphere of a residential area.

non_diegetic_music: Minimalist ambient cinematic soundtrack with a warm sustained low cello tone and subtle resonant piano notes fading gently at the end.

nodes.title: README
widgets_values:
* **FL2V (Frame-to-Video):** This mode offers simplicity, primarily focusing on generating video from single frames. Options include using only the first frame, only the last frame, or both simultaneously. The “Last Frame” option has limitations regarding resizing; I’ve configured it to forcefully truncate the image based on the dimensions of the first frame if enabled. There are inherent constraints related to latent size and the corresponding resolution of the first/last images – they should ideally be consistent. While minimal differences in resource allocation generally don't impact generation, drastically different aspect ratios (e.g., album-style starting image and portrait-oriented final image) can lead to unexpected results. I haven’t yet discovered a more robust solution without disrupting the generation process. ## Video Resolution Logic (FL2V Model) The target resolution is determined by the first available input in the following fallback order: 1. **First Frame** (with optional **Last Frame**) * The **First Frame** is resized to the user-defined resolution (both dimensions divisible by 32). * If **Last Frame** is provided: It is strictly forced to match the exact dimensions of the processed **First Frame** (using the **fill/crop** method). This is highly recommended to prevent dimension mismatches if the source images differ in size. 2. **Last Frame** ONLY (No **First Frame**) * The Last Frame is resized to the user-defined resolution (both dimensions divisible by 32). * Note: It is recommended to use the **keep proportional** resize method for this specific node. 3. **Text-Only** (No images provided) * The user-defined resolution is automatically rounded to ensure both width and height are divisible by 32.
odel preview (latent preview) adds some time to generation and the more preview_frames used, the stronger the effect.
